# Attributes {#attributes}

An attribute line applies only to the block on the next line, and an attribute block in running text attaches only to a span, link, image, code span, math, footnote reference, symbol or closed emphasis (C2-B-091, C2-I-036). Attribute text that 0.1 dropped without a trace now stays visible.

**U-282** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-I-042, an empty or blank `class` value: `{class=""}` above `p`, `{class=" "}`
Tool: An empty value adds no class, so no element carries `class=""`: `<p>p</p>`. No 0.2 source writes the empty attribute.

::: compare no-render
```text
{class=""}
p
```
```text
<p>p</p> The value of a `class` key is split at runs of spaces and tabs and an empty value adds no class (C2-I-042), so no element gets `class=""`; 0.1 wrote the value as authored, also `class=" "`. No 0.2 source writes an empty `class` attribute.
```
:::

**U-283** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-H-167, an empty `rel` on a link: `[x](/u){rel=""}`
Tool: A link carries no `rel` when nobody gives a word: `<a href="/u">x</a>`. No 0.2 source writes the empty attribute.

::: compare no-render
```text
[x](/u){rel=""}
```
```text
<p><a href="/u">x</a></p> A link carries no `rel` when neither the author nor the profile gives a word (C2-H-167); 0.1 wrote `rel=""` as authored. No 0.2 source writes an empty `rel` attribute.
```
:::

**U-392** <Badge type="info" text="none" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> An uppercase attribute name: `{CLASS=z}` on a line block. 0.1 writes `CLASS="z line-block"`; 0.2 writes `class="z line-block"`, the same HTML attribute.

:::: compare no-render
```text
{CLASS=z}
::: |
verse
:::
```
```text
<div class="z line-block">
  <p>verse</p>
</div> Attribute names are written once in their canonical case under C2-H-012 and C2-H-013. HTML attribute names are not case-sensitive, so the tool compares them lowercased and the old `CLASS` output is the same attribute.
```
::::
